transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-10-14 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Sanjay Patel (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (CTO, Cygnus AI), Mark Hudson (VP Eng), Ethan Park (Platform Eng)

Summary: Quick discovery to understand Cygnus's reliability requirements for their customer-facing inference endpoints. Focus on how Redwood handles incidents, automatic fallbacks, multi-region routing, and SLA commitments; also touched on Private/VPC needs and compliance.

[00:00] Sanjay: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. quick intros - I'm Sanjay, AE at Redwood, and Maya's our systems lead. can you do quick intros?
[00:12] Lena: Yeah hi I'm Lena, CTO. we run the inference platform for Cygnus, mostly latency-sensitive APIs for our customer chat and personalization.
[00:18] Mark: Mark, VP Eng, overseeing infra and SRE. main thing for us is availability and incident tolerance.
[00:24] Ethan: Ethan, platform eng, I own routing and deployment automation.
[00:29] Maya: Great, thanks. high level - we typically ask about QPS, tail latency targets, tolerance for brief quality/regression tradeoffs during failover, and compliance.
[00:39] Lena: We're aiming for p95 < 250ms for single-turn inferences, and p99 ideally under 600ms. but availability is critical, we want no more than 15 minutes of customer-facing degradation — that's our internal SLO.
[00:51] Sanjay: Got it. and what's your expected QPS and peak patterns?
[00:56] Ethan: steady 1200 qps across east and eu regions, spikes to ~4k during launches — so autoscaling and region-level failover are important.
[01:06] Maya: ok makes sense. two quick clarifying q's — do you have a hard restriction on sending data to third-party clouds or are you ok with hosted in our managed environment?
[01:15] Lena: For EU data, must stay within EU region; for some enterprise customers we need private deployment or a VPC option.
[01:22] Mark: Also KMS integration is required for customer-sensitive keys and audit logs. SOC2 is a checkbox for procurement.
[01:30] Sanjay: That aligns with our Hosted + Dedicated + Private options. Hosted can be regionally isolated and we provide KMS integrations, Dedicated gives reserved capacity with stronger isolation and SLA, and Private gives customer-controlled networking.
[01:43] Maya: On incident tolerance — would you describe the desired failure model? e.g., do you want automatic fallback to a smaller model, cross-region traffic shift, or a degraded response mode?
[01:53] Mark: Ideally automatic routing to another region if a region goes down, fallback to a lighter model if latency spikes, and a graceful degradation mode (partial responses) only if absolutely necessary.
[02:05] Lena: And we want seamless observability — traces, per-token costs, and rollback hooks.

---
[02:20] Maya: Quick architecture sketch: Redwood supports smart routing policies — you can prefer region, prefer cost, or prefer latency. on incident, we support automatic cross-region failover, and can fallback to compatible model variants (quantized/lower-capacity) with policy controls. We also expose hooks for canary rollouts and automatic rollback.
[02:40] Ethan: When you say "compatible model variants", how do you handle differences in tokenization/behavior between variants? we can't have large regressions.
[02:48] Maya: good q. we recommend pinned model families and version mapping; the runtime supports function-level equivalence checks and you can configure acceptance thresholds. we also support routing to an evaluation tier where responses are scored against a golden dataset before full flip. it's not perfect but reduces surprise regressions.
[03:09] Mark: what's the failure detection time, and how fast is the cross-region failover?
[03:15] Maya: failure detection is configurable — heartbeat and latency health checks. typically detection within 10-30s and traffic shift in under 90s for simple failovers. for more conservative settings you can tune that.
[03:29] Lena: 90s for traffic shift is ok, but the end-user experience during that interval is a concern. do you provide circuit-breaker or retryable client libraries?
[03:39] Sanjay: We provide SDKs with retry/backoff and also server-side circuit breaker controls. plus you can use per-route fallbacks to return cached results for known prompts or a quick summary.

[03:52] Ethan: about SLA – what SLA do you put on Hosted vs Dedicated? we need numbers to present to our procurement team.
[03:59] Sanjay: Hosted standard SLA is 99.5% monthly uptime with a best-effort latency target; Dedicated gets higher guarantees — 99.9% and packet-level latency commitments depending on plan. for enterprise Private deployments we can negotiate a tailored SLA. I'll send the SLA matrix after this call.
[04:16] Mark: Any penalties or credits?
[04:18] Sanjay: yes, standard SLA credits for Dedicated, details in the docs. will include in the pack.

[04:26] Maya: another operational detail — KV cache warmup across regions. when failing over, cold KV caches can add latency. we support prefix-level caching replication options for hot keys, or you can accept a brief cold-cache penalty.
[04:39] Ethan: Can we TTL-map cache entries to be replicated proactively?
[04:42] Maya: yes, TTL and replication policies available. recommended for session-heavy workloads.

[04:50] Lena: For security, you mentioned KMS and HSM. we need BYOK and audit logs forwarded to our SIEM.
[04:58] Sanjay: BYOK supported in Dedicated and Private. audit logs can be forwarded to your syslog/S3 with retention controls. we'll include exact API endpoints in the security pack.

---
[05:12] Mark: let's talk about POC. what would you need from us to validate failover behavior?
[05:18] Maya: ideally test dataset and QPS profile, specify regions (we can run across us-east-1 and eu-west-1), and success criteria: failover time under 120s, p95 latency degradation no more than 2x baseline, and no more than 5% request error rate during failover.
[05:34] Ethan: we can provide 10k-sample prompts and simulate traffic to 2-3k qps for spikes.
[05:40] Lena: timeline — procurement needs SOC2 docs before Dedicated contract, but we can run a Hosted-regioned POC first.
[05:48] Sanjay: totally reasonable. Hosted-regioned POC to validate routing and fallback behaviors, then escalate to Dedicated for SLA and BYOK.

[05:57] Maya: regarding cost tradeoffs — automatic cross-region failover increases egress and instance-hours. for Dedicated you can reserve burst capacity to avoid cold spin-ups. we also recommend quantized model variants for cost-sensitive fallbacks.
[06:10] Mark: ok, so we need a clear cost estimate for a worst-case failover scenario.
[06:14] Sanjay: we'll run a cost model in the pack.

[06:20] Ethan: do you support weighted routing so we can split traffic eg 80/20 for blue/green across regions during slow rollouts?
[06:27] Maya: yes, weighted routing and traffic shaping are supported. you can also define blackout windows and automatic rollback thresholds based on error rates or quality metrics.

[06:38] Lena: on the audit side — can logs include per-token cost attribution? procurement asked for chargeback visibility.
[06:45] Sanjay: yes token-level cost and latency breakdowns per request are available in the Console and exportable via API.

---
[06:55] Mark: any references for customers running multiregion setups or similar failover tests?
[07:00] Maya: we've done a few case studies; I'll include redacted benchmarks from two customers with similar p95 targets.
[07:06] Lena: sounds good. also want to clarify how model compatibility is surfaced — e.g., if we fallback to a quantized 4-bit variant, will prompts and outputs match closely?
[07:16] Maya: generally yes for most prompt types, but differences can appear in nuanced reasoning. we recommend evaluation prompt sets and automated regression checks as part of the rollout.

[07:27] Ethan: operational runbook — would Redwood provide an incident runbook template for failover and rollback?
[07:33] Sanjay: yes, we provide runbook templates, playbooks, and we can run a joint tabletop exercise during the POC.

---
[07:42] (short side conversation, coffee noises)
[07:50] Lena: one procurement note — we need data residency certification for EU and a contact for security questionnaire.
[07:57] Sanjay: I'll share the security pack and put Maya on the loop for technical Q&A.

[08:03] Maya: quick technical note — if you want near-zero RPO for cache, we can replicate hot prefixes asynchronously to reduce write amplification; that raises cost but lowers failover tail-latency.
[08:16] Mark: good to know, include cost delta.

[08:22] Ethan: can we test simulated region outage rather than real outage? we prefer controlled chaos testing.
[08:27] Maya: absolutely; we'll run controlled failover tests and simulate region blackholes in the POC harness. results will include latency, error rates, and cost impact.

[08:36] Lena: if POC looks good, what are typical lead times for Dedicated? we have a busy quarter.
[08:41] Sanjay: Dedicated procurement and capacity allocation typically 4-8 weeks depending on GPU availability and contract. Private/on-prem takes longer due to infra setup.

[08:49] Mark: last question — do you offer any SLA-backed fallbacks? meaning if a Redwood region is unavailable and we experience >X downtime, are there guarantees on cross-region failover effectiveness?
[08:60] Maya: (laughs) note timestamps — so we can include formalized failure modes in Dedicated contracts. for Hosted we publish best-effort, for Dedicated we add defined failure mode responses and credits. we'll include sample SLR (service-level response) clauses in the SLA pack.

---
[09:15] Sanjay: ok let's recap and action items. we'll: 1) send pricing/SLA matrix; 2) share security/compliance pack; 3) Maya will draft a POC plan for multiregion failover including metrics and test harness; 4) Cygnus to confirm dataset and QPS profile and procurement requirements.
[09:34] Lena: +1. mark/ethan will coordinate the dataset and access.
[09:39] Mark: thanks, looking forward to the POC details.
[09:42] Ethan: thanks everyone.
[09:44] Sanjay: great, we'll follow up by EOD with the initial docs. thanks!

(Conversation continues with brief clarifications, timestamps omitted to keep things concise)

End of transcript.
